name: maximum_entropy_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, a 5-second return that falls beyond the 95th percentile of the past 5-minute return distribution represents a statistically anomalous flush of market orders — typically cascading stop-loss triggers or short-term momentum algos overshooting on thin liquidity. The maximum entropy distribution (approximated via Cornish-Fisher expansion using rolling mean, std, and skewness) correctly identifies when positive or negative skew makes an event truly extreme rather than just 'large under a normal assumption.' Within 30-90 seconds, NIFTY's structural mean-reversion forces (VWAP-anchored institutional accumulation, market-maker delta-hedging from gamma exposure) fade these overshoots. Entering at the close of the extreme bar — while still below VWAP for longs, above VWAP for shorts — captures the early phase of the reversion before it completes.

indicators.name: ret_5s
indicators.purpose: Raw 5-second return — the signal input. Original used 1-min returns; we use 5s returns because we are detecting micro-level tail events that resolve within 30-90 seconds.

indicators.name: roll_mean_60
indicators.purpose: 60-bar (5-minute) rolling mean of 5s returns. Chosen as 5 minutes rather than the original's 60-minute window because we need the current micro-volatility regime, not the full-session average. A 60-minute window would blend morning gap-fill volatility with afternoon calm, blurring the threshold calibration. 60 bars also provides enough data points (60 observations) for reasonable skewness estimation.

indicators.name: roll_std_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute rolling standard deviation. Same window as roll_mean_60 — they must be computed on the same sample for the distribution to be internally consistent.

indicators.name: roll_skew_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute rolling skewness — the critical improvement over simple z-scores. NIFTY intraday returns exhibit negative skew during sell-offs (many small positive returns, occasional large negatives) and positive skew during trending up days. The Cornish-Fisher expansion uses this to shift the tail thresholds asymmetrically, avoiding false 'extreme' signals on the fat-tail side of the distribution.

indicators.name: maxent_p5_cornish_fisher
indicators.purpose: Cornish-Fisher approximation of the MaxEnt P5 threshold. The CF expansion adjusts the normal quantile by skewness without requiring numerical optimization, making it stable and fast at 5s bar frequency.

indicators.name: maxent_p95_cornish_fisher
indicators.purpose: Cornish-Fisher P95 threshold. When a 5s return exceeds this level, it is in the top 5% of the past 5-minute distribution — statistically extreme relative to the current regime.

indicators.name: session_vwap
indicators.formula: cumsum(close * volume) / cumsum(volume), reset each day
indicators.purpose: Cumulative session VWAP as a directional anchor. VWAP-benchmarked algos accumulate below VWAP and distribute above VWAP, making VWAP a structural mean-reversion attractor. VWAP below-close filter prevents fading a strong trend: we only buy CE after an extreme DOWN move when price is below VWAP (aligning with the VWAP reversion pull), and buy PE after an extreme UP move when above VWAP.

conditions: ret_5s < maxent_p5_cornish_fisher (extreme negative 5s return — bottom 5% of recent distribution)
close < session_vwap (price below VWAP, structural mean-reversion pull is upward)
vix_close < vix_max=22 (elevated VIX causes frequent extremes, degrading signal quality)
roll_std > 0 (sufficient recent volatility for meaningful distribution fitting)
buy_ce.confirmation: Signal fires at bar close — no extra confirmation to avoid missing fast reversions

conditions: ret_5s > maxent_p95_cornish_fisher (extreme positive 5s return — top 5% of recent distribution)
close > session_vwap (price above VWAP, structural mean-reversion pull is downward)

exit.stop_rationale: 3 option points = ~6 spot points retracement. If a NIFTY 5-second extreme return (which is itself ~8-15 spot points at the P5/P95 level) continues to deepen by another 6 spot points rather than reverting, the thesis is wrong — momentum has overwhelmed mean-reversion. At delta ~0.5, 3 option pts = 6 spot pts, consistent with a maximum acceptable adverse continuation within our 30-90s hold window.
exit.target_rationale: 5 option points = ~10 spot point reversion. Statistical tail events on NIFTY (P5/P95 at 5-min distribution) typically overshoot by 8-15 spot points and revert 60-80% within 60-90 seconds — capturing 10 spot pts (5 option pts) is the lower bound of the expected reversion (1:1.67 R:R). This is calibrated against the 30-90s window where NIFTY reversion averages 8-12 pts (4-6 option pts).

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 22 — in high VIX regimes, tail events occur frequently (multiple per hour) and do NOT revert reliably; the statistical rarity that makes them meaningful breaks down
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (need 60-bar warmup from 09:20 open for distribution estimation) or after 15:20
filters.volume_filter: None — NIFTY volume is institutional-dominated and poorly correlated with mean-reversion quality at 5s
filters.trend_filter: Implicit via VWAP — only enter in direction of VWAP reversion, avoiding strong trend continuation
filters.spread_filter: None — limit order execution, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: Moderate — the Cornish-Fisher skewness adjustment is a genuine statistical improvement over simple z-scores, but if NIFTY's 5-minute return skewness regime shifts (e.g., post-news), the threshold calibration can lag by 2-5 minutes

adaptation_notes: The original strategy operated on NIFTY 50 constituent stocks individually. The core idea — using maximum entropy distribution fitted to rolling moments rather than a naive normal assumption — translates directly to the NIFTY index return series. Key changes: (1) Timeframe compressed from 1-min to 5s bars, lookback compressed from 60-minute to 5-minute window (different reasoning: we need the current micro-volatility regime, not a multi-hour average); (2) MaxEnt optimization replaced with Cornish-Fisher approximation for numerical stability at 5s frequency; (3) Universe dependency removed — one index, not 50 stocks; (4) Stock-specific filters (volume, bid-ask spread on individual stocks) replaced by NIFTY structural filter (VWAP position); (5) Mean-reversion thesis preserved — statistically extreme returns revert, and the skewness-adjusted threshold correctly identifies 'truly extreme' vs 'extreme under normal assumption.'
weaknesses: 60-bar window (5 minutes) provides only marginal statistical power for skewness estimation — requires ~100+ observations for reliable skewness; use CF adjustment as directional bias, not precise quantile
NIFTY index 5s returns have very thin tails at short lookbacks — P5/P95 may be triggered by routine 3-5 spot point moves during low-volatility periods, generating noise signals
Mean-reversion at 30-90s can fail on macro event days (RBI announcements, budget, global shock) when the 'extreme' return is information-driven, not noise; no event filter implemented
